senses.sense_definition: A variety of a language specific to a particular region or social group, differing in grammar, vocabulary, or pronunciation.

examples.text: The local <w>dialect</w> is difficult for outsiders to understand.
Many <w>dialects</w> of English exist across the United States.

senses.sense_definition: A language variety contrasted with a standardized form of the same language.

examples.text: Linguists often study how a <w>dialect</w> differs from the standard language.
Some people wrongly believe that a <w>dialect</w> is just a broken version of a language.

senses.sense_definition: Speech perceived as non-standard or socially inferior.

examples.text: The teacher told the students that they should not speak <w>dialect</w> in the classroom.
He felt ashamed to speak his native <w>dialect</w> in professional settings.

senses.sense_definition: A specific version or variant of a programming language.

examples.text: This code uses a specific <w>dialect</w> of SQL that is only supported by this database.
The software supports several <w>dialects</w> of the BASIC programming language.

senses.sense_definition: A distinct variation in the vocalizations of a bird species within a specific population.

examples.text: Researchers discovered that birds in different forests sing in unique <w>dialects</w>.
The song of this species shows a clear <w>dialect</w> depending on the region.
